objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. The ordination hall of a wat and its visual anchor. A stepped white terrace and plinth with a stair at each end; thirty red columns forming a peristyle round a solid white hall body with eight windows a side and a door at each end; a hipped portico skirt over the colonnade; a 45-degree middle roof layer; a top gable telescoped into three sections, centre highest; glazed eaves bands, white risers and bargeboards, red trim, carved gilt pediments in both end gables; sixteen curved horns; and eight bai sema boundary stones. The registry notes are explicit that the sema are what make this an ORDINATION hall rather than a general assembly hall, so they belong to the asset and are not optional dressing.

reasoning: The identity is the ROOF, and it is not a stack: a hipped portico skirt round the colonnade, a 45-degree middle layer the full 18 m of the core, and a top gable TELESCOPED along the length into a 12 m centre with its ridge at 14.8 m and two 3 m ends at 14.0 m -- read off the proxy's side elevation, where the layer lines run continuous and only the ridges step.
Five repetition systems: thirty columns, sixteen chofa and rake-foot horns, sixteen window surrounds, sixteen window leaves and eight boundary stones. Every one is instanced.

Material layering is seven -- stone, red lacquer, tile, olive glaze, gilt, shade and the carved pediment canvas -- because a Thai temple roof is genuinely polychrome, and four of them carry post-construction weathering canvases.
Action readiness is minimal: static landmark geometry, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The roof cannot be expressed as nested full gables, and it cannot be expressed as one prism either: the layers step in plan on the SIDE slopes while the end gable is a single triangle from the middle layer's eaves to the ridge, and the ridge itself steps along the length. Each layer is therefore three solids -- a white riser, a glaze band, a tile field -- and the gable ends are their own slabs following the stacked outline.

silhouette.description: A stepped white platform to 1.30 m, a red colonnade to 6.9 m between white pedestals and capitals under a 37-degree portico skirt whose eaves are at 7.2 m with long 27-degree end hips, then the roof core TELESCOPED on both registers: a 45-degree middle layer from 9.0 to 10.85 m over the 12 m centre and 8.65 to 10.5 m over the 2.5 m ends, and a top gable whose ridge is 14.8 m over the centre and 13.85 m over the ends, with the centre's stepped gable faces showing above each end section. Every panel is framed in glazed green -- eaves band, top strip, rake stripes -- with gilt bargeboards and spiral horns at every gable apex (to 16.9 m), every rake foot and every skirt corner. The silhouette events are the colonnade's rhythm, the three roof registers, the telescoped ridge and the horns breaking every edge of the roofline.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -6.95..+6.95 (the portico skirt's eaves fascia at hw 6.94 and the terrace at 6.85), z spans -12.00..+12.00 set by the bottom terrace, y spans 0.00 to 16.92 set by the tip of the centre-ridge chofa. The declaration was CHANGED for this rebuild: the first build was declared 12 x 12 x 24 and the Meshy proxy of the same plate normalises to long:h:short = 1 : 0.709 : 0.573, i.e. 24 x 17.0 x 13.7 m. The registry now declares 14 x 17 x 24, and every height here is read off the proxy's two orthographic elevations at that scale.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to long:h:short = 1 : 0.709 : 0.573. The first build was declared 1 : 0.5 : 0.5 and its area-weighted band comparison read mean |delta width| 0.173 and |delta depth| 0.446 of height -- the largest divergence of the monumental set, almost all of it that one ratio. This rebuild re-declares the envelope from the proxy and reads every register off its orthographic elevations (scratch/_mon/front.mjs, side and end): skirt eaves hw 6.8, middle eaves hw 5.0 at 9.0 m, top eaves hw 3.1 at 10.9 m, ridges 14.8 / 13.85 m, apex chofa to 17.0 m. THIRD BUILD: the proxy side elevation, scanned column by column (43 px/m), puts the centre ridge at 14.72 over x 0..6, the end ridges at 13.84 over x 6.1..8.9, and the skirt hip at 7.66 m at x 9.3 falling to 7.1 at x 10.2 -- a 31-degree end hip, far shallower than the 37-degree sides -- so the top register was shortened to 17.0 m (bands 7-8 read the old 17.9 m 0.08-0.10 H long), the skirt eaves raised to 7.2 with the hip top pulled in to 7.8, and the middle register telescoped with the top. The band table now reads mean |delta width| 0.014 and |delta depth| 0.029 of height, from 0.017 / 0.044; the residual is band 7 width (+0.05, the gilt bargeboards and horns at 12-13.6 m, which the proxy fuses thin) and band 4 depth (+0.06, the raised skirt eaves now falling inside the band).

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.80: the hall is bilaterally symmetric on both axes, the plate shows two adjacent elevations, and the Meshy proxy is symmetric end to end with a stair and doorway at both ends, which is also the convention for the type.

repetitionSystems.name: Peristyle columns
repetitionSystems.rationale: Thirty columns at ONE geometry and ONE submission, counted off the plate's right-hand elevation. As separate meshes they would exceed the whole draw-call budget on their own.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Column heads are buried in the eaves beam, which is 0.05 m proud of their outer faces; feet stand on the cap course as an opposed butt.

repetitionSystems.name: Column capitals and pedestals
repetitionSystems.rationale: The plate's columns are red BETWEEN two white blocks: a pedestal continuous with the parapet and a capital under the eaves beam. One unit of two boxes on the column grid, thirty instances, one draw call; the second build had bare shafts.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Both blocks are 0.085 m proud of the shaft on every side and their faces sit inside the beam and above the cap course, so no face shares a plane.

repetitionSystems.name: Chofa and rake-foot horns

placement.note: One apex chofa per gable (four), one horn at each rake foot of each gable (eight), one at each hip corner of the skirt (four). Each instance carries its own yaw, rise and hand.

repetitionSystems.rationale: The registry notes call the horn finials the feature that separates an ubosot from any other rectangular hall. Sixteen of them cost one draw call; the apex chofa are scaled to 2.35 m so the centre one sets the declared height.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Ten tapering segments along a heading turning from 68 to 118 degrees -- past 90 the tip curls BACK, the plate's S-shaped chofa, where the second build's sine arc was a spike. No two segments are parallel, so nothing inside the unit can share a plane.

repetitionSystems.name: Window surrounds

placement.note: Eight bays a side between the columns, at z +-1.02, +-3.06, +-5.10, +-7.14, on both long faces.

repetitionSystems.rationale: One surround geometry for all sixteen windows, at one draw call.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Back face on the wall face as an opposed butt; the leaf's back on its front face likewise.

repetitionSystems.name: Window leaves

placement.note: Centred on each surround, standing 0.03 m proud of it.

repetitionSystems.rationale: Its own system because it is its own material; sixteen leaves at one draw call.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Proud of the surround, never sunk into it.

repetitionSystems.name: Bai sema boundary stones

placement.note: On the bottom terrace outside the plinth: four at the corners, two at the mid-sides, one centred before each stair.

repetitionSystems.rationale: Pedestal, plinth and pointed leaf blade merged into one unit, eight placements. These are required by the registry notes and not optional dressing.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: The blade is an extruded curved leaf on a two-step pedestal; each step is narrower than the one below, so they meet as opposed faces, and every pedestal stands clear of the plinth face.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero4x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Ten components and six repetition systems: 16 of 24. The columns are the expensive lesson avoided -- thirty of them would exceed the draw-call budget on their own -- and the sixteen windows would have doubled the count again as separate meshes.

materials.note: stone covers the platform, the body, the risers, the gable walls, the column capitals, the window surrounds AND the boundary stones; red covers the columns and all the trim; gilt the sixteen horns AND the bargeboards; carved the four pediments. Seven of sixteen materials, and the seven are genuinely seven finishes -- a Thai temple roof is polychrome by construction.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 5,496 of 32,000. Prisms, quad strips and boxes, with the horns as ten-segment spirals; nothing here is expensive. The tile course and the pediment carving that the first build declared lost to the budget are both here, as canvases costing no triangles at all.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Extruded prisms, quad-strip rings, and boxes rotated to the rake. The roof is the interesting case: a hipped skirt has to be a ring of trapezoids because an extrusion gives vertical ends; the layers above it are truncated gable cross-sections extruded along the hall, with the top gable cut into three extrusions of different ridge height so the roof telescopes.

Six InstancedMesh systems carry 116 of the prop's 162 discrete parts. The horn system uses a per-instance yaw, a per-instance rise and a NEGATIVE X scale for the opposite hand, which is what lets one geometry serve every apex, rake foot and hip corner.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless, and four seamless Canvas 2D tiles are bound AFTER construction as map and bumpMap: streaked whitewash on the stone, peeling lacquer on the red (re-based to the plaster envelope so the flakes can be brighter than the base), laid tile courses with moss on the terracotta and the glaze, and the carved gilt pediment. Every tone is a measured display-space ratio; dark cores are held above the hole gate; the whole set builds in under 70 ms and 5.3 MB of texture VRAM.
